summary: ig-gox executes an obfuscated embedded payload at import time behind anti-analysis guards
details: The pypi package ig-gox ships a top-level ig_gox/__init__.py that, on import (the README's documented usage), base64-decodes a ~5 KB embedded blob, XOR-decrypts it with a hardcoded key, zlib-decompresses it, HMAC-verifies it, then exec/compiles the resulting Python under __name__='__main__'. The visible wrapper has no other functionality; all actual behavior of the package is contained in that concealed blob. Before decoding, the module performs anti-analysis checks: it calls sys.exit(0) if sys.gettrace() returns a tracer, if the process environment/cwd/argv contain substrings such as 'uncompyle', 'pycdc', 'decompyle', 'deobfuscate', 'hook', or 'frida', and it tampers with references to builtins.exec/eval/compile. The combination of a hidden exec-of-decoded-payload reached automatically on import and explicit evasions against debuggers and decompilers is deliberate concealment of code execution from the installer and from reviewers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
